title: dnspython text-format WKS records can exhaust memory and CPU
summary: An unchecked WKS service number causes oversized bitmap allocation and inefficient growth when parsing attacker-controlled DNS record text. Resource exhaustion can terminate the process.

severity.rationale: Developer or agent DNS tooling must parse attacker-controlled zonefile-format records to be exposed. The documented impact is denial of service, warranting a 30-day response.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.

exposure: The attacker must control record type and rdata text passed to the zonefile-format parser. This advisory does not establish exposure through ordinary DNS wire-format replies.

remediation.details: Use 2.9.2 or later. The fixing release requires Python 3.11 or later.
remediation.risk: Medium if the application still uses an older Python interpreter; validate dependencies before upgrading.

verification: Confirm the loaded dnspython version is 2.9.2 or later and run normal zonefile parsing checks.
